questions.prompt: What is the total running time of the KMP string-matching algorithm on a text of length n and pattern of length m?
questions.explanation: KMP scans the text once (the text pointer never moves backward) after O(m) preprocessing, giving O(n + m) total.

questions.prompt: What does the prefix (failure) function of a pattern store for each prefix?

options.text: The length of the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix
The number of distinct characters in the prefix
The index of the pattern in the text

questions.explanation: The prefix function captures the pattern's internal repetition — the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix — enabling the fallback on a mismatch.

questions.prompt: Which statements about string matching are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Naive matching is O(nm) in the worst case
KMP never moves the text pointer backward
Naive matching is always faster than KMP

questions.explanation: Naive is O(nm) worst case, KMP is linear and never rescans the text. Naive is not always faster — it can be far slower on repetitive input.

questions.prompt: KMP precomputes the ______ function (also called the failure function) of the pattern. (one word)
questions.explanation: The prefix function tells KMP how far to fall back within the pattern on a mismatch without re-reading text.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of the KMP algorithm.

items.text: Compute the prefix function of the pattern
Scan the text left to right, advancing the pattern pointer on matches
On a mismatch, fall back the pattern pointer via the prefix function (text pointer stays)
Report a match when the whole pattern is matched

questions.explanation: KMP preprocesses the pattern, then scans the text once, using the prefix function to fall back within the pattern instead of rescanning the text.

questions.prompt: Match each algorithm/term with its fact.

pairs.right: O(n + m) using the prefix function
Longest proper prefix that is also a suffix

questions.explanation: Each matcher trades preprocessing for search speed; the prefix function is the structure that powers KMP.
